Overall, while the analysts have reconfirmed their revenue estimates, the consensus now no longer provides an EPS estimate. This implies that the market believes revenue is more important after these latest results.

There's been no real change to the consensus price target of US$77.41, with Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile seemingly executing in line with expectations. The most important thing to take away is that the analysts reconfirmed their revenue estimates for next year, suggesting that the business is performing in line with expectations. data.title: We Think vTv Therapeutics (NASDAQ:VTVT) Can Afford To Drive Business Growth

We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although software-as-a-service business Salesforce.com lost money for years while it grew recurring revenue, if you held shares since 2005, you'd have done very well indeed. Nonetheless, only a fool would ignore the risk that a loss making company burns through its cash too quickly.

Given this risk, we thought we'd take a look at whether vTv Therapeutics (NASDAQ:VTVT) shareholders should be worried about its cash burn. For the purposes of this article, cash burn is the annual rate at which an unprofitable company spends cash to fund its growth; its negative free cash flow. We'll start by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves in order to calculate its cash runway.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

How Long Is vTv Therapeutics' Cash Runway?

A company's cash runway is calculated by dividing its cash hoard by its cash burn. In September 2026, vTv Therapeutics had US$77m in cash, and was debt-free. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through US$22m. That means it had a cash runway of about 3.6 years as of September 2026. A runway of this length affords the company the time and space it needs to develop the business. Depicted below, you can see how its cash holdings have changed over time.

How Is vTv Therapeutics' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Whilst it's great to see that vTv Therapeutics has already begun generating revenue from operations, last year it only produced US$37m, so we don't think it is generating significant revenue, at this point. Therefore, for the purposes of this analysis we'll focus on how the cash burn is tracking. Over the last year its cash burn actually increased by 4.3%, which suggests that management are increasing investment in future growth, but not too quickly. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but investors should be mindful of the fact that will shorten the cash runway. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

How Hard Would It Be For vTv Therapeutics To Raise More Cash For Growth?

While its cash burn is only increasing slightly, vTv Therapeutics shareholders should still consider the potential need for further cash, down the track. Generally speaking, a listed business can raise new cash through issuing shares or taking on debt. One of the main advantages held by publicly listed companies is that they can sell shares to investors to raise cash and fund growth. By comparing a company's annual cash burn to its total market capitalisation, we can estimate roughly how many shares it would have to issue in order to run the company for another year (at the same burn rate).

Since it has a market capitalisation of US$204m, vTv Therapeutics' US$22m in cash burn equates to about 11% of its market value. Given that situation, it's fair to say the company wouldn't have much trouble raising more cash for growth, but shareholders would be somewhat diluted.

How Risky Is vTv Therapeutics' Cash Burn Situation?

As you can probably tell by now, we're not too worried about vTv Therapeutics' cash burn. For example, we think its cash runway suggests that the company is on a good path. data.title: Tesla (TSLA) Could Be 42% Undervalued Following SpaceX Merger Talk
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) is back in the spotlight after reports that it is in advanced merger talks with SpaceX on a possible multi trillion dollar combination focused on AI, robotics and transportation.

The merger speculation is landing at a tricky time for Tesla investors. The 1‑day share price return declined 7.64% and the 7‑day move is down 11.38%, extending a year‑to‑date share price fall of 21.06%, even though the 3‑year total shareholder return is up 46.88%.

Scan how other AI and robotics contenders are pricing in similar storylines by running Tesla alongside a hand picked set of 53 AI infrastructure stocks.

Tesla now trades about 17% below the average analyst target after a sharp pullback, even as rumours of a SpaceX tie up keep expectations high. Is that discount enough to reflect the risks the market is flagging?

Most Popular Narrative: 42% Undervalued

Tesla closed at $345.82 while the most followed Simply Wall St Community narrative pegs fair value at $600.82, implying a large gap that frames how some investors are reading the SpaceX merger talk.

According to Ledora, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the key question is whether Tesla's big product stories can justify that kind of valuation gulf over time.

Tesla remains an interesting stock to watch as investors weigh its long-term growth potential against near-term execution risks. Robotaxi development, Optimus, energy storage and vehicle demand are all important parts of the company''s future, but profitability and cash flow will ultimately determine how sustainable that growth becomes.

See why 38 investors see Tesla as 42% undervalued.

The discount rate used in the narrative is 10.46%, which sets a relatively demanding hurdle for future cash flows yet still supports a fair value well above the current price. That reflects an outlook where the AI, autonomous driving, energy storage and robotics efforts eventually contribute meaningfully on top of the existing $103.57b revenue base and $3.22b in net income, even though profit margins of 3.1% are currently below last year's 5.3%.

At the same time, the narrative sits against some tougher cross-checks. The SWS DCF model suggests Tesla is trading above an estimated future cash flow value of $188.47 and recent statements highlight weaker earnings over the past year and a lower return on equity of 3.6%. That kind of split view is why the merger speculation with SpaceX matters so much for sentiment, because any credible path to higher, more durable profits becomes central to whether a $600.82 fair value feels realistic.

Result: Fair Value of $600.82 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, Tesla faces real pressure if vehicle margins stay thin or if AI and robotics projects take longer than expected to translate into solid earnings.

Another View: Tesla’s Price Versus Sales

The narrative fair value of $600.82 for Tesla leans heavily on long term potential. A simple P/S yardstick paints a very different picture. At 13.2x sales, TSLA trades far above the US Auto industry at 0.4x, peers at 1.1x, and a fair ratio of 3.2x.

That kind of gap means even small disappointments in execution or SpaceX merger expectations could have an outsized impact on the share price, while stronger than expected progress might already be partly reflected in today’s valuation. data.title: Selling Kingsway Shares at a Lower Price Than Current Market Value May Have Been a Costly Mistake for Insiders
data.description:
Even though Kingsway Corporation (NYSE:KWY) has fallen by 10% over the past week , insiders who sold US$657k worth of stock over the past year have had less luck. Insiders might have been better off holding onto their shares, given that the average selling price of US$12.51 is still below the current share price.

Although we don't think shareholders should simply follow insider transactions, we would consider it foolish to ignore insider transactions altogether.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Kingsway

Earlier in the year, they sold shares at a price ofUS$13.32 per share in a -US$400k transaction. While insider selling is a negative, to us, it is more negative if the shares are sold at a lower price. It's of some comfort that this sale was conducted at a price well above the current share price, which is US$8.10. So it is hard to draw any strong conclusion from it.

In the last twelve months insiders purchased 9.01k shares for US$97k. But insiders sold 52.50k shares worth US$657k. All up, insiders sold more shares in Kingsway than they bought, over the last year. The average sell price was around US$12.51. We are not joyful about insider selling. But the selling was at much higher prices than the current share price (US$8.10), so it probably doesn't tell us a lot about the value on offer today. You can see a visual depiction of insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last 12 months, below. If you want to know exactly who sold, for how much, and when, simply click on the graph below!

Check out our latest analysis for Kingsway

For those who like to find hidden gems this free list of small cap companies with recent insider purchasing, could be just the ticket.

Kingsway Insiders Bought Stock Recently

We saw some Kingsway insider buying shares in the last three months. Insiders purchased US$25k worth of shares in that period. It's great to see that insiders are only buying, not selling. However, in this case the amount invested recently is quite small.

Insider Ownership

I like to look at how many shares insiders own in a company, to help inform my view of how aligned they are with insiders. I reckon it's a good sign if insiders own a significant number of shares in the company. It appears that Kingsway insiders own 19% of the company, worth about US$45m. We've certainly seen higher levels of insider ownership elsewhere, but these holdings are enough to suggest alignment between insiders and the other shareholders.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Kingsway Insiders?

Insider purchases may have been minimal, in the last three months, but there was no selling at all. The net investment is not enough to encourage us much. Our analysis of Kingsway insider transactions leaves us cautious. But we do like the fact that insiders own a fair chunk of the company. So these insider transactions can help us build a thesis about the stock, but it's also worthwhile knowing the risks facing this company.
